problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: The stated global strong-convexity inequality implies convexity on all of E.

problem_class.label: strongly_convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a differentiable μ-strongly convex function f:E→ℝ, with 0<μ≤L and an attained global minimum x*. The initial objective gap satisfies f(x0)−f(x*)≤Δ.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: A query x returns ∇f(x) exactly for every call index and seed. There is no oracle error or sampling dependence in the reply, and no function-value oracle is supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/NormalizedSamStronglyConvex.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, and final clause of spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is an arbitrary real Hilbert space. The gradient is globally L-Lipschitz. E, L, x0, μ, ρ, Δ, and ε are public, with ρ>0, Δ≥0, and ε>0; f and its minimizer are hidden. The setup restricts allowed algorithms to the named NormalizedSam.method family with some fixed η>0 and the supplied ρ and x0.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned point must satisfy f(output)−f(x*)≤ε after the fixed exact-gradient call budget.

accuracy.label: almost_sure

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Smooth strongly convex minimization with exact gradients and an objective-gap target is a classical formulation. The named algorithm-family restriction specifies which methods may witness the guarantee. descriptionHtml:
Normalized SAM for Strongly Convex Minimization

We consider minimizing a differentiable function f:E→R on a real Hilbert space E using normalized sharpness-aware minimization (SAM). The function is μ-strongly convex with L-Lipschitz gradient, where 0<μ≤L. A given starting point x0∈E satisfies f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ for a global minimizer x⋆ and Δ≥0. The oracle returns ∇f(x) at x. With perturbation radius ρ>0 and tolerance ε>0, the goal is a last iterate x¯ satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ on E. The algorithm receives E, L, μ, ρ, x0, Δ, and ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E, and ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈E.

Assumption 2 (Strong convexity). For every x,y∈E, f(y)≥f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+μ2∥y−x∥2.

Assumption 3 (Minimizer and initial gap). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ.

Our result is algorithm-specific: we analyze normalized SAM with a fixed step size η>0, chosen from the available inputs, and the prescribed radius ρ. Starting from the given x0, the method uses two successive gradient queries per iteration: gt=∇f(xt),ut={gt/∥gt∥,gt≠0,0,gt=0,yt=xt+ρut,xt+1=xt−η∇f(yt),t=0,1,2,…. Queries may be made at any point of E. The step size remains constant throughout the run. For an oracle-call budget N∈{0,1,2,…}, the output is x¯=x⌊N/2⌋. If N is odd, the final call evaluates the gradient at the current iterate without completing another update. The required accuracy is f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
Differentiable f on a complete real inner-product space, with L-Lipschitz gradient, μ-strong convexity, a minimizer x⋆, and f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ; 0<μ≤L, ρ>0, Δ≥0, ε>0. Exact gradients are available. The setup requires constant-step normalized SAM with radius ρ and last-state output. Result (1) uses η=(2L+2L2ρ/με)−1 and guarantees f(xK)−f(x⋆)≤ε deterministically.

(3) GD (Karimi et al. 2016, Thm. 1). E=Rd; problem-class comparison without the SAM restriction. O(1+κℓ) (1): No established improvement. (1) adds κ3/2ρL/εℓ; dominant when ρ≫με/L. Two gradient calls per step instead of one.
(4) AGD (Nesterov 2018, sec. 2.2, Thm. 2.2.1, Lem. 2.2.4). E=Rd; problem-class comparison without the SAM restriction. O(1+κℓ) (1): No established improvement. (1) has κ instead of κ, plus the radius term; at least a κ cost gap when Δ≥ε.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex

namespace LongTails.Algorithms.NormalizedSam

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]

noncomputable def method (η ρ : ℝ) (x0 : E) : OracleTemplate.Algorithm E E E 1 where
  State := E × E × Bool
  initial _ := (x0, 0, false)
  query s := (0, if s.2.2 then s.1 + (ρ / ‖s.2.1‖) • s.2.1 else s.1)
  update s reply := if s.2.2 then (s.1 - η • reply, 0, false) else (s.1, reply, true)
  output s := s.1

noncomputable def step (g : E → E) (η ρ : ℝ) (x : E) : E :=
  x - η • g (x + (ρ / ‖g x‖) • g x)

noncomputable def output (g : E → E) (η ρ : ℝ) (x0 : E) (T : ℕ) : E :=
  (step g η ρ)^[T] x0

end LongTails.Algorithms.NormalizedSam

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.NormalizedSamStronglyConvex

structure Params extends LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex.Public where
  μ : ℝ
  ρ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : OracleTemplate.Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := (p.E → ℝ) × p.E
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.μ ∧ p.μ ≤ p.L ∧ 0 < p.ρ ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p I oracle :=
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt I.1 (gradient I.1 x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient I.1 x - gradient I.1 y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ x y, I.1 x + ⟪gradient I.1 x, y - x⟫ + p.μ / 2 * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2 ≤ I.1 y) ∧
    IsMinOn I.1 Set.univ I.2 ∧ I.1 p.x0 - I.1 I.2 ≤ p.Δ ∧
    (∀ k x seed, oracle.answer k (0, x) seed = gradient I.1 x)
  successful p I output P :=
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), I.1 (output ω) - I.1 I.2 ≤ p.ε
  allowedAlgorithm p A :=
    ∃ η : ℝ, 0 < η ∧ A = LongTails.Algorithms.NormalizedSam.method η p.ρ p.x0

end LongTails.Setups.NormalizedSamStronglyConvex
